title: Hunt Instead of Wait: Evaluating Deep Data Research on Large Language Models
claim: Compared with earlier tasks, our open-ended task maximizes exploration and agency, and the benchmark has components that fit into one evaluation pipeline.
layout: 2 panels: left staircase on interaction-agency axes, right component system diagram
description: The figure has two halves split by a dashed vertical line. The left half is a 2-D plot with Agency on the x-axis and Interaction on the y-axis, and a large gray curved arrow rising to the upper right. Four small gray cards sit along the arrow, from bottom to top: NL2SQL (Model as Translator), Table QA (Model as Reasoner), AI4DS (Model as Analyst) and Deep Data Research (Model as Researcher). Each card has a mini-flow of boxes such as Query, Model, Evaluation and Answer. The cards get more complex going up. The right half is the DDR-Bench overview, with a legend of icons across the top. Blue boxes for Database (structured data and freeform reports) feed a Checklist Generator and Human Expert Screening. In the middle, an agent loop of reasoning, tool-use and observation steps runs over an MCP Server, a ReAct Agent and an LLM backend. This loop produces Agent-Mined Insights, which go into a pink Evaluation box with example insights and an example checklist verification. The eye goes first to the large Evaluation and Database boxes.
caption: Left: Compared with previous tasks, DDR maximises exploration openness and agency, focusing on the direct evaluation of insight quality. Right: Overview of the DDR-Bench. Details of the trajectory samples are shown in Appendix [ref].
abstract: The agency expected of Agentic Large Language Models goes beyond answering correctly, requiring autonomy to set goals and decide what to explore. We term this investigatory intelligence, distinguishing it from executional intelligence, which merely completes assigned tasks. Data Science provides a natural testbed, as real-world analysis starts from raw data rather than explicit queries, yet few benchmarks focus on it. To address this, we introduce Deep Data Research (DDR), an open-ended task where LLMs autonomously extract key insights from databases, and DDR-Bench, a large-scale, checklist-based benchmark that enables verifiable evaluation. Results show that while frontier models display emerging agency, long-horizon exploration remains challenging. Our analysis highlights that effective investigatory intelligence depends not only on agent scaffolding or merely scaling, but also on intrinsic strategies of agentic models.
